data.title: Face ID Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone 11 comes with a distinct feature named Face ID. Where it uses the iPhone user's face to unlock the phone. This feature was made available from the iPhone X models and the later Apple A12x Bionic chipsets. The Face ID feature uses the true depth, dual front cameras provided with the iPhone as the basic instrument for this feature. It also emits an infrared laser to convert your distinct and unique facial features into geometrical and mathematical data for the iPhone.

Face ID is a very complex technology, and users might often misinterpret one of its features as an error in the technology. Here are some common issues regarding the iPhone’s Face ID feature.

  • Face not recognized
  • Face ID is not available at the moment
  • Move the camera a bit lower/higher
  • Upon Unlocking iPhone directly takes me into Passcode and not Face ID

These common issues however have some home remedies which may work for your iPhone. These fix attempts are risk-free and do not risk damaging your phone.

  • Check if your face ID is on for iPhone Unlock. Go to: Settings > Face ID and Passcode
  • if you use a screen protector make sure it doesn’t obstruct the front camera in any way.
  • Make sure you face the camera and nothing is covering or obstructing between your face and camera region.
  • Restart your phone. Make sure there is no dirt or your front camera lens is not foggy.
  • Update your iOS to the latest version.

If your phone doesn’t unlock with Face ID instead prompts with a passcode. The reasons may be:

  • User might be wearing a face mask while opening the iPhone.
  • The user may have just restarted the device.
  • The phone has not been unlocked in more than 48 hours.
  • The passcode has not been used to unlock the phone in the last 7 days.
  • The device has not been unlocked by face ID in the last 4 hours.
  • The iPhone has a remote lock on and is away from safe space.
  • If a user fails to unlock the device after five unsuccessful face ID unlock attempts.
  • If at Face ID set up, your iPhone shows or tells you to move the device lower or higher. Chances are that the Device does not support face ID at all

If your iPhone 11 Face ID problems can’t be categorized and sorted by the above-mentioned issues and fixes, you may just need to take it to an extremely diligent iPhone technician to deal with Face ID issues. data.title: Error Solution
data.description:
Sometimes when you update your iPhone, or when you try to run your phone you may see some sort of black screen with some sort of Error with a number on your iPhone’s screen out of nowhere. These messages with errors and numbers can be seen while booting up the phone or trying to upgrade the ipsw files from iTunes from a pc. These are Error Codes that indicate to the service technicians that a specific part of the iPhone is malfunctioning. These codes are used by professional repair technicians of iPhones to make their jobs easy. They do not need to diagnose the entire iPhone when they see the code. Therefore, saves both the customer’s and the tech expert’s time and other resources.

Some of the common error codes seen in the iPhones are as follows:

ERROR(9): This code shows when you are trying to upgrade your iOS through PC on iTunes, but the iTunes app shows an Error code-9. It is a relatable problem with iTunes error codes – 4013, 4014, and 4005.

Apple recommends:

To check if your iPhone is updated

To check if the lightning cable works. (Error code 4013,4014 and 4015 usually indicate this issue)

If the update still fails try updating from another pc.

Error 1015: This is an issue if you have a jailbroken device (iOS) and apple detects it.

Error 69: This is a common issue found in iPhone X and later devices. This issue suggests that there might be some sort of hardware error on your phone, which is repairable, to say the least.

Aside from these errors, there are a lot of errors that can occur on your iPhone. These are all listed on Apple’s error solution info pages with possible DIY (Do it yourself) solutions.

  • Phone gets hot and the battery drains drastically.
  • You might see a notification that will say “Temperature high”
  • The iPhone gets warm on standby mode for no apparent reasons whatsoever.

(Note: if your phone gets too hot while transferring data for the first time from a previous iPhone, chances are it’s a one-time issue and will not happen again.)

  • Disable background app refresh.
  • Disable background app refresh from here: Settings > General > Background App Refresh
  • Turn off Bluetooth / Location services to reduce processes running in the background
  • Most of the users have reported they get the heating issue in the latest iOS version, In that case,

data.title: Charge Draining Issue
data.description:
The battery is optimized perfectly for the phone. However, it may be for some manufacturer error or something about some faulty apps’ optimization, you may not get the smoothest output from your iPhone 11 battery. Most users have reported that the iPhone’s battery starts draining after the system has updated to iOS 14 Several other issues may cause battery drain issues also. These issues include:

  • The battery of the iPhone 11 runs out too quickly after the update
  • The battery of the iPhone 11 runs out after installing an app/ update of an app
  • The battery of the iPhone drains quickly after turning on the optimized charging mode
  • The iPhone Battery drains after the phone heats up too quickly

These are the most common problems regarding battery-draining found on the internet. Your issues may be one of them or not listed! However, we recommend trying some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes that may resolve your issue.

  • Turn off background iCloud/iTunes sync to save battery by a considerable amount.
  • When not in use turn off WiFi/Cellular Data/Location/Bluetooth service in your iPhone
  • Don’t overcharge/ Frequently charge your iPhone 11. It may reduce battery health.
  • Turn on optimized battery charging to save your battery life and protect it from draining.
  • Adjust your brightness settings in iPhone 11 to auto-brightness.
  • Turn off Background app refresh
  • From here: Settings > general > Background app refresh
  • Try running it on low power mode
  • from here: Settings > Battery > Low power mode ON
  • Turn off “reduce motion” to turn off aesthetic animations in your phone to save battery life might help
  • Turn it off from here: Settings > General > Accessibility > Reduce Motion

If none of the aforementioned procedures work to resolve your battery draining issues, it may need to be looked at by a professional technician to get them resolved. data.description:
The new iPhone 11 offers its users better optimization and balance in software than the previous iPhone models. However, no matter hard they try there can always be some technical issues that can result in your iPhone malfunctioning. The Apple logo stuck issue was also found in previous iPhones and it’s a frustrating issue. Your iPhone boots up, but instead of going to the home screen, it is stuck on the boot menu. This problem happens mainly/most of the time because of a software issue that happens due to an unclean or interrupted update.

This Stuck on Apple logo issue might happen in other instances too. Possible reasons might be:

The iPhone has taken in some physical damage. (Dropping from hand)

The update was disrupted due to Wi-Fi disturbance/metered connection or cellular data loss.

A third-party app may have access to vital permissions which can disrupt iPhones' productivity.

It is rare; however, your phone might be facing a hardware issue. Sometimes faulty hardware prevents the phone from booting up.

These issues however can be resolved if it is just a bug or a glitch in the iOS software. You may try the following steps and see if it works for you.

Force Restart your iPhone 11

(Press volume up (+) and then quickly press volume down (-) button and hold the iPhone 11 power button as long as the apple logo appears again)

Update your iOS Software.

(If, while in the progress of updating your software, the progress bar under the Apple logo has not moved for an hour, you may connect your iPhone to a PC and select “Update” when prompted)

Remove all third-party apps from your phone. Install Apps only from the Apple App store

Turn off the auto-update of your iOS apps to prevent further interruptions. BUT BE SURE TO UPDATE THEM ON A REGULAR BASIS MANUALLY.

data.title: Liquid Damage
data.description:
The new iPhone 11 is a standard IP68 rated, dust and water-resistant phone. This means it can resist dust and water coming in up to a certain level. However, it is not completely immune to water getting inside the iPhone and damaging it. Apple has introduced a new technology called LCI. LCI is an abbreviation for liquid contact indicator. It is located in the sim tray region. Now you can see the LCI when you remove the sim tray, buy putting the ejector pin into the sim tray ejection hole. Once you have removed the sim tray, you should see a white/red portion inside the sim tray region. That is your LCI on the iPhone. If the LCI is completely white or silver then it is okay. The phone hasn’t contacted any water.

However, if your LCI turns red you can safely assume that it has been in touch with water and has taken in some water damage.

If you have dropped your phone in the water here are some basic things you should do:

  • Rinse your phone with a lens cloth or a microfiber cloth
  • You may gently tap the phone with the charger hole against your hand. It may drip the water out if it has gotten in there.
  • NEVER CHARGE YOUR PHONE UNTIL YOU HAVE MADE SURE IT IS COMPLETELY DRY

If anything spills on your phone other than water (like oil etc.) just rinse the place with a lint-free cloth. If water has gotten into your phone, it may damage your Battery, Charging port, or give you muffled speakers. then:

Make sure your Data connection is on after setting up the network before you access the internet.

Restart your iPhone

  • The battery charges very slowly
  • iPhone 11 not charging beyond 80 %.
  • Charging Not available or Liquid has been detected in the charging port error.

If your phone has any one of these issues or something not mentioned in the list of the common issues. You will still like to check out these DIY (Do it yourself) fixes that may solve the problem regarding the charging dock in your iPhone 11.

  • Make sure you don’t have any debris or dirt on your charging dock. This may prevent charging.
  • Make sure your power outlet isn’t faulty.
  • Make sure you do not have the “optimized battery charging” option checked on your iPhone 11. if you do have it make sure to disable it to charge your phone past 80%.
  • Disable optimized Charging in here: Settings > Battery > Battery Health.
  • Note: This option is only available on iOS 13 or later updates.

data.description:
The new iPhone 11 offers one of the best displays consisting of a Liquid Retina IPS LCD display and a significantly high DPI. It has also ensured maximum safety for its users by putting gorilla glass in both the back and front. The No light on Display issue of the iPhone 11 is where the user can’t see what’s happening on the phone. The phone runs okay. The phone vibrates and the user can hear the notification sounds and other inputs.

But the problem is they can not see any of it because the phone display is just plain black. But the phone will respond or might even have incoming calls.

The key symptoms of the “No light on Display” issues are:

  • The Phone display boots up with an Apple logo but doesn’t get past the black screen (iPhone 6 – 8Plus)
  • The phone has calls, notifications but doesn’t show anything on display
  • iPhone can charge (you can hear the sound that the phone makes while charging) but won’t show anything on the display.
  • This “No light on display” is usually an internal issue with the LCD connector. However, Apple recommends some processes to practice on your phone to make sure the black screen is not a software glitch.
  • Force Restart your iPhone.

(Press the volume up (+) and volume down (-) and then press and hold the power button until the Apple logo appears on the screen)

  • Connect the lightning cable, charge it for 10 minutes. Then try force restarting the iPhone.
  • UNCONVENTIONAL: But press the screen into the phone so it may reconnect any dislodged LCD connector. This fix is not recommended however it resolved a lot of the user's Black Display issue. It might be risky for any layman person.

data.description:
The Taptic Engine in an iPhone Xs is responsible for providing haptic feedback, such as vibrations for notifications and the "click" sensation for the home button (on supported models). You might need to replace the Taptic Engine in your iPhone if you experience any of the following issues:

Signs You Might Need to Replace the Taptic Engine:

  • If your iPhone stops providing vibrations or feedback for notifications, calls, or system interactions.
  • The Taptic Engine works only occasionally or inconsistently.
  • The Taptic Engine produces grinding or buzzing noises that were not present before.
  • Error messages or diagnostics indicate an issue with the Taptic Engine.

Possible Causes of Failure:

  • Physical Damage: Dropping the phone or exposing it to water can damage internal components.
  • Software Bugs: Sometimes, a software issue may mimic hardware failure. Perform a factory reset or update the iPhone before deciding on hardware repair.
  • Wear and Tear: Over time, mechanical components can degrade and stop working properly.
